# testdata

Golden vectors shared by the Rust, TypeScript, and Lean suites:

- policy documents (canonical JSON) and their expected `doc_hash`:
  `ci-publish.*`, the primary External-signer document;
  `ci-publish-delegated.*`, the same document with the ci signer as a
  CAP-0071 delegated address; `ci-publish-threshold.*`, the same document
  with the publish rule as a 1-of-2 `threshold` quorum carrying a `cap`;
  `ci-publish-recovery.*`, the same document enrolling guardian-only
  `protected` recovery with a baseline; `ci-publish-recovery-combined.*`,
  the same document enrolling combined guardian+ZK `loss` recovery with no
  baseline (lost-key only). The `recovery` member's schema is
  [`../docs/recovery/spec.md`](../docs/recovery/spec.md) §3.1.
- `rule-hashes.json`: the per-rule canonical hash (`CANONICAL.md`, "Fragment
  hashes") of every rule in the three non-recovery fixtures, generated by
  `../scripts/rule-hash-vectors.py`
- `recovery/statement-v2.json`: recovery statement, credential, replacement
  set, and ZK projection vectors ([`../docs/recovery/statement.md`](../docs/recovery/statement.md)),
  generated by an independent implementation,
  `../scripts/recovery-statement-vectors.py`
- recovery members on their own (`recovery/config-{guardian-only,zk-only,combined}.canonical.json`):
  `recovery_canonical_json`, the text `config_hash` commits to
  ([`../docs/recovery/spec.md`](../docs/recovery/spec.md) §3.2), one per mode.
  Generated by `crates/perch-ir/tests/recovery.rs` from the recovery fixtures
  above (zk-only takes the guardian-only document with the combined one's ZK
  factor; Rust and the Lean model only). Regenerate with
  `PERCH_BLESS=1 cargo test -p perch-ir --test recovery`
- `auth/auth-vectors.json`: the signing digest OZ checks signatures
  against, OZ's `AuthPayload` as an auth entry carries it, and the contract
  error codes perch-js maps to typed errors, written from the account's own
  types by `crates/integration-tests/tests/auth_vectors.rs`
  (`PERCH_BLESS=1`)
- `auth/diagnostic-events.json`: the host's own diagnostic events for the
  submission failures perch-js types, written by
  `crates/integration-tests/tests/revision.rs` (`PERCH_BLESS=1`)
- `eval/eval-vectors.json`: hand-authored `(program, invocation) → verdict`
  cases replayed by the Rust evaluator, the compiled Wasm, and the Lean
  model ([`../docs/verification/PLAN.md`](../docs/verification/PLAN.md))
- `zk/`: one real ZK proof per recovery scenario, with the enrollment
  history to rebuild its pool, generated by `perch-zk-fixtures` with the
  pinned toolchain (`docs/zk/README.md`)
- `golden/`: byte-level XDR of the on-chain wire format
  ([`golden/README.md`](golden/README.md))

The canonical JSON / `doc_hash` bytes these vectors pin are defined normatively
in [`../CANONICAL.md`](../CANONICAL.md) (CANON v1). Every `*.canonical.json`
here and under `recovery/` is also parsed and re-emitted byte-identically by
the Lean model's verified canonicalizer (`just drt`, and the `formal` job in
`.github/workflows/assurance.yml`). A change to
`ci-publish.canonical.json` or `ci-publish.doc-hash` is a canonical-form break
and requires a `CANON_VERSION` bump.

## `deploy/`: not golden vectors

`deploy/` holds the deployment PolicyDoc template
(`perch-testnet.template.json`) and the infra list
`scripts/bootstrap-testnet.sh` publishes content-addressed
(`constructorless-manifest.json`). The bootstrap writes the per-network documents
it generates from the template (`perch-testnet.json`,
`perch-testnet.rules.json`) next to them; those are not committed. These
files are environment-specific, expected to change, and pinned by nothing.
The frozen-vector rules above do not apply to this subdirectory.
